abstract: Research on synthetic respondents has concentrated on fidelity: how closely AI-generated answers match those of human panels. This note asks how organisations use a synthetic panel once they have accepted it. We analyse the usage logs of one provider: 895 survey projects run by 24 enterprise teams between May 2024 and October 2026. Projects fall into two clusters of similar size: testing (52%), dominated by concept screens set up mostly by research functions, and developing (47%), descriptive questions about customers and markets set up almost entirely outside research. Across the data corpus, 70% of projects were set up outside the research function and the median project reached results in 3.9 hours. On this basis, we propose the concept of synthetic micro-research: fast market research on synthetic panels set up primarily by non-researchers, which we hypothesise serves low-stakes decisions that would otherwise have gone untested. The note closes with a research agenda for synthetic research in use and implications for corporate research functions and agencies.

title: Synthetic Micro-research: What Organisations Ask once Respondents Cost Nothing
